title: _eager_execute rebuilds node_map manually instead of using the cached graph.node_map property
description: Line 1327 constructs `node_map = {n.id: n for n in graph.nodes}` inside the preamble-error injection block. PipelineGraph already exposes `node_map` as a @cached_property whose body is exactly `{n.id: n for n in self.nodes}` (src/haute/_types.py:697-700), and execute_graph itself uses `graph.node_map` (executor.py:1082). The manual rebuild duplicates that logic and rebuilds the dict on every preamble-error path instead of reusing the memoised mapping. Replacing it with `node_map = graph.node_map` is behaviour-preserving (the cached_property returns the same mapping for the same instance) and removes the hand-rolled comprehension.
evidence: executor.py:1327 `node_map = {n.id: n for n in graph.nodes}` vs _types.py:698-700 `@cached_property def node_map(self): return {n.id: n for n in self.nodes}`. The surrounding loop (1328-1331) only reads node_map.get(nid), so the cached property suffices.
est_reduction: 1 line (replace comprehension with cached-property access); avoids a redundant dict build on preamble-error paths.
behavior_preservation: Identical mapping content; cached_property is computed from the same graph.nodes and is read-only here.
